introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) specified in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 00/0595/3/Grp 1, Grp 2, Grp 3 and Grp 4). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (documents, workbooks and pictures supplied in the candidate folder) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Carry out the following formatting instructions.

- Add horizontal borders for the cells in the ranges A3:E3, A13:E13 and A15:E15  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **A3:E3**, hold **Ctrl** and select **A13:E13** and **A15:E15**. *Home* > **Borders** (the list next to the border button) > **Top and Bottom Border** (or *All Borders* if the horizontal lines above and below each row are wanted). A horizontal line now frames each of the three rows (headings, total of expenses, total income).

*Marking idea (2 marks):* the three ranges selected (1); horizontal borders applied (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: - Merge the cells in the range A1:E1  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **A1:E1** and click **Merge & Center** (*Home* > *Alignment*). The five cells become one cell that holds the heading BUDGET FOR THE TERM.

*Marking idea (1 mark):* A1:E1 merged.

questions.enonce_markdown: - Format the heading to Bold and a size of 20 points  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click the merged heading cell (A1), click **Bold** (Ctrl+B) and choose **20** in the *Font Size* box.

*Marking idea (1 mark):* bold and 20 points.

questions.enonce_markdown: - Format the cells in the range B4:E15 to use the thousands separator and zero decimal place when displaying numbers  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **B4:E15**, then *Home* > *Format Cells* > *Number* > **Number**, set **Decimal places: 0** and tick **Use 1000 Separator (,)** (or click the **Comma Style** button and remove the decimals with *Decrease Decimal*). The numbers are then displayed as 150,000 and 20,000 and so on, with no decimal part.

*Marking idea (3 marks):* range B4:E15 selected (1); thousands separator (1); zero decimal places (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: - Set the horizontal alignment of Cells B17:E17 to Centre.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **B17:E17** and click **Center** (*Home* > *Alignment*), or *Format Cells* > *Alignment* > *Horizontal: Center*. The comments that the IF formulas will display in row 17 are then centred in their cells.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* B17:E17 selected (1); horizontal alignment set to centre (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Use the Sum function at Cell E4 to sum the contents of the cell range B4:D4. Copy the formula down to cell E11, and also to cells E13 and E15.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**E4: `=SUM(B4:D4)`**

Select E4 and drag the fill handle down to **E11**; the references move with the row (E5 is `=SUM(B5:D5)`, ..., E11 is `=SUM(B11:D11)`). Copy E4 (Ctrl+C) and paste it (Ctrl+V) into **E13** and **E15**, where it becomes `=SUM(B13:D13)` and `=SUM(B15:D15)`.

Results (recalculated with Python): E4 to E11 = 150000, 20000, 45000, 6000, 1500, 75000, 15000, 20000 (displayed 150,000, 20,000, 45,000, 6,000, 1,500, 75,000, 15,000, 20,000); E13 = 332,500 once row 13 is filled (question 5); E15 = 352,500 (250,000 + 50,000 + 52,500).

*Marking idea (3 marks):* SUM function with the range B4:D4 (1); copied down to E11 (1); copied to E13 and E15 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Compute the Jan expenses in Cell B13. Copy the formula in Cells C13 and D13, to do the computation of expenses for Feb and Mar.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The expenses of January are the sum of the expense lines of column B, from row 4 to row 11:

**B13: `=SUM(B4:B11)`** = 222,500

Copy B13 to **C13** (`=SUM(C4:C11)` = 57,500: the School Fees and Books cells of February are empty) and **D13** (`=SUM(D4:D11)` = 52,500).

Check for January: 150000 + 20000 + 15000 + 2000 + 500 + 25000 + 5000 + 5000 = 222500.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* formula for Jan (1); copied to C13 and D13 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Use the **IF** function in Cell B17 to display the message **OK** if the expenses for Jan are less than or equal to income for Jan, otherwise, display the message **OVERDRAWN**  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The test compares the expenses of January (B13) with the income of January (B15). The two messages are text, so they are written between double quotation marks:

**B17: `=IF(B13<=B15,"OK","OVERDRAWN")`**

Jan: 222,500 <= 250,000 is true, so B17 displays **OK**.

*Marking idea (3 marks):* IF function with the test B13<=B15 (1); value if true OK in quotation marks (1); value if false OVERDRAWN (1).

- **E4: `=SUM(B4:D4)`**
- **B13: `=SUM(B4:B11)`**
- **C17: `=IF(C13<=C15,"OK","OVERDRAWN")`** (the formula of B17 copied one cell to the right: the references B13 and B15 become C13 and C15)

Value of C17: C13 = 57,500 and C15 = 50,000. As 57,500 is greater than 50,000, the test is false and C17 displays **OVERDRAWN**. For March, 52,500 <= 52,500 is true, so D17 (copy of B17) displays **OK**: the *less than or equal to* includes the case of equality.

*Marking idea (3 marks):* one mark for each correct formula.
